body:
With NX8's 8-bit static formats, the tensor that loses most even in its best format is layernorm output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256: 32.1 dB SQNR (signal-to-quantization-noise ratio; higher is better) in fp8_e2m5, measured on that tensor alone by the format search. Measured on 12 models with a format search (of 279 surveyed).

Model outputs keep a median 23.2 dB SQNR against full precision, the worst 12.8 dB (stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae). 8 of 10 models with a prediction metric (top-1, perplexity or agreement) lose some of it; the most: microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (agreement 100% → 0%: the share of samples whose predicted class matches full precision's), PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (agreement 100% → 58%: the share of samples whose predicted class matches full precision's) and stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (token agreement 100% → 66%: the share of token positions whose predicted token matches full precision's).

The tensors that lose most in their best format (their own error): layernorm output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 32.1 dB), linear bias in SamLowe/roberta-base-go_emotions (fp8_e2m5, 33.6 dB), add output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 34.0 dB), layernorm bias in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e3m4, 34.2 dB), mul output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 34.5 dB), layernorm bias in openai-community/gpt2 (fp8_e3m4, 34.5 dB), linear bias in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e2m5, 34.7 dB), layernorm output in SamLowe/roberta-base-go_emotions (fp8_e3m4, 35.3 dB), layernorm output in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e3m4, 35.5 dB) and linear output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 35.5 dB).

Separately, the error accumulated along the data path (every tensor before a node quantized too): div outputs end furthest from full precision, microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition keeping only -inf dB there. The outputs furthest from full precision in each model's best format set: div in microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (fp8_e3m4, -inf dB), linear in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, -3.0 dB), sub in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, -2.4 dB), softmax in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, -1.1 dB), relu in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, -1.1 dB), mul in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, -0.8 dB), div in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, -0.0 dB), mul in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, 0.5 dB), aten in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, 0.9 dB) and sum in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, 1.2 dB).

Formats chosen (E = exponent bits, M = mantissa bits, u = unsigned): fp8_e2m5 4577 (55%), fp8_e3m4 2687 (32%), fp8_e1m6 1056 (13%), ufp8_e2m6 71 (0.85%), ufp8_e1m7 3 (0.04%), ufp8_e3m5 2 (0.02%); 0.91% of tensors use an unsigned format.

body:
3 missing capabilities keep 35 operations in 6 models (of 11 planned) off the chip's direct path; the most widespread is run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip) (32 operations in 5 models). Ranked by the MACs they hold:

**Run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip).** The chip cannot read memory at an address computed at run time, so every lookup or choice by a run-time value (embedding) needs a workaround. It affects 32 operations in 5 models: 32 calls (0.83% of all calls) and no MACs (data movement only); the biggest: embedding in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256, embedding in SamLowe/roberta-base-go_emotions and embedding in openai-community/gpt2. Cost today: 0 of 32 have a workaround (0 exact, 0 approximate), 2 failed and 30 wait for one; 85 workarounds proposed, 15 passing its check, 16 evaluated on a model; accuracy not measured yet; cycles not measured yet; 0 extra kernels.

**An integer format for indices.** No NX8 format can hold an integer index computed from the input, so the operations reading one (add and gather) need a workaround. It affects 2 operations in 1 model: 2 calls (0.05% of all calls) and no MACs (data movement only); the biggest: add in SamLowe/roberta-base-go_emotions and gather in SamLowe/roberta-base-go_emotions. Cost today: 0 of 2 have a workaround (0 exact, 0 approximate), 0 failed and 2 wait for one; 0 workarounds proposed, 0 passing its check, none evaluated on a model; accuracy not measured yet; cycles not measured yet; 0 extra kernels.

**An aten::conv1d instruction.** The chip has no instruction for aten::conv1d, so every aten::conv1d needs a workaround. It affects 1 operation in 1 model: 1 call (0.03% of all calls) and MACs not counted (the capture does not size an ATen op); the biggest: aten::conv1d in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese. title: Missing instructions: 35 operations in 6 models need workarounds

body:
A kernel reads a tensor in the arrangement its writer stored it in; when the reader needs another arrangement, the reading kernel has to rearrange the data itself. This happens to 669 of 1108 tensors passed between kernels (60%) in 11 models: 485 for attention heads split or merged, 163 for other reshapes, 18 for pixels reordered and 3 for image patches.

The reading operations are 439 operations (439 calls, 11% of all calls; 104 G MACs, 4.19% of all MACs). The most common causes (writer → reader): linear → bmm (attention heads split or merged) 262, linear → attention (attention heads split or merged) 207 and linear → add (other reshapes) 64; most in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (202), stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (128) and jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (87).

Cost today: extra cycles not measured yet (no reading kernel has run); 0 links fail.
title: Layout conversions: 669 of 1108 tensors between kernels are rearranged

body:
Activations such as exp, GELU and reciprocal go through a 256-entry lookup table (LUT), which limits their precision: 1,088 operations in 11 models (1,088 calls, 28% of all calls), most often layernorm (324), silu (210) and groupnorm (113). Their quantized accuracy: worst -inf dB SQNR over 1,025 measured operations.

Kernels per forward pass (host launches, one per planned kernel call): median 22, most 82 (stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5, 82 planned groups), over 11 models.

FP32 headroom (how far the largest value is from FP32 overflow, in powers of ten) is least at 33.4 powers of ten for bmm in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (largest value 1.35e+05).

13 outputs in 1 model hold a value at the FP32 limit itself (mostly add (12) and select_where (1), e.g. an attention mask's fill value); they are counted apart from the headroom.

2 accuracy runs produced non-finite outputs (overflow or NaN).

0 kernels use over 80% of the 1,024-word instruction memory (IMEM) bank, of 1 kernel measured.
title: Resource limits: 1,088 operations limited by the LUT and up to 82 kernel launches per pass

body:
**Most costly: compute efficiency.** Binary is the worst case — across 14 measured cases it keeps only 0% of the multipliers busy (0% MAC utilisation), so the pipeline cannot feed the multipliers at all, and it accounts for 100% of the on-chip cycles among the 4 operations in 1 model measured on chip.

**Second: NX8 format accuracy.** Across 12 models (280 surveyed), model outputs keep a median 23.2 dB SQNR vs full precision with a worst of 12.8 dB; 8 of 10 models with a prediction metric lose some of it, most severely microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (agreement 100% → 0%). The tensors losing most in their best format are layernorm output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (32.1 dB), linear bias in SamLowe/roberta-base-go_emotions (33.6 dB) and add output in DiT-XL-2-256 (34.0 dB); accumulated data-path error is worse still, with div in table-transformer at −inf dB.

**Third: resource limits.** 925 operations (28% of calls) in 9 models are constrained by the 256-entry LUT (worst −inf dB SQNR over 862 measured), kernel launches reach a median of 22 and up to 82 per pass, and 2 accuracy runs produced non-finite outputs.

**Fourth: layout conversions.** 546 of 947 tensors (58%) between kernels must be rearranged by the reader, mostly for attention head split/merge (377), affecting 352 calls (11%) holding 102 G MACs (4.22%); cycles are not yet measured.

**Least costly: missing instructions.** Run-time addressing is the only missing capability, blocking 29 calls (0.89%, no MACs — data movement only) in 4 models, all embeddings; 0 of 29 have a working workaround today, but adding it would put all 29 on the chip directly.
title: GLM summary

body:
**Run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip)** would put 32 operations in 5 models on the chip directly, with no workaround: 32 calls (0.83% of all calls) and no MACs (they only move data); the accuracy it would recover is not measured yet (no workaround evaluated).

**An integer format for indices** would put 2 operations in 1 model on the chip directly, with no workaround: 2 calls (0.05% of all calls) and no MACs (they only move data); the accuracy it would recover is not measured yet (no workaround evaluated).

**An aten::conv1d instruction** would put 1 operation in 1 model on the chip directly, with no workaround: 1 call (0.03% of all calls) and MACs not counted (the capture does not size an ATen op); the accuracy it would recover is not measured yet (no workaround evaluated).
